column5: Reflection anchor with 32k second LR drop
column6: A 32k second LR drop flattened late training and peaked at 93.33%, below the reflection-padding anchor baseline.
Symmetric padding preserved throughput but peaked at 93.48%, below the reflection-padding anchor and the 93.68% improvement threshold.

Lower smoothing nearly cleared the bar at 93.79%, but the +0.09 gain remains noise under the +0.10 rule.

column5: 22k first LR drop on label-smoothed anchor
column6: A 22k first drop matched 93.79% but stayed inside the noise band, so 21k remains the label-smoothed anchor.

column5: Lower smoothing plus 22k first LR drop
column6: Combining the two 93.79 near-misses regressed to 93.63%, so their effects are not additive.

column5: Batch size 112 on label-smoothed reflection anchor
column6: Batch size 112 preserved the first LR drop but cut useful coverage to 39,859 steps and plateaued at 93.43%.

column5: Weight decay 2e-4 on label-smoothed reflection anchor
column6: Stronger weight decay improved the label-smoothed reflection anchor to 93.97%, showing the current wider recipe benefits from more shrinkage.

column5: Weight decay 3e-4 on label-smoothed reflection anchor
column6: Weight decay 3e-4 over-regularized the current anchor, dropping best accuracy to 93.55%; keep 2e-4 as the stronger-decay anchor.
Higher LR 0.12 added noisy high-LR training and peaked at 93.70%, so the 2e-4 anchor should keep LR 0.1.
Reducing weight decay to 1.5e-4 weakened the 2e-4 anchor, peaking at 93.61%; keep 2e-4 as the local decay setting.
Mild mixup could not produce a valid final metric because both local attempts were interrupted before best_test_acc was reported.
Lowering initial LR to 0.08 undertrained the pre-drop phase and peaked at 93.49%, so LR 0.1 remains the anchor.
Mild RandAugment reached 93.83% but stayed below 94.07%, adding runtime without clearing the improvement threshold.

column5: Sparse late EMA after first LR drop
column6: Sparse late EMA activated but collapsed to 89.07%, showing buffer/averaged-weight mismatch remains severe.
Elapsed-time cosine completed cleanly but plateaued at 93.01%, below the step-schedule anchor and 94.07% threshold.
Under GPU contention, mild ColorJitter missed the 21k LR drop and peaked at 88.89%, so this run is no-improvement but weak attribution.
Lower BatchNorm momentum smoothed eval statistics but underperformed the anchor at 93.48%, so default BN momentum remains preferable.
Decoupled weight decay preserved throughput but weakened the 2e-4 anchor, peaking at 93.06% below the 94.07% threshold.
Clean ColorJitter reached the 21k LR drop but still peaked at 93.49%, so mild photometric augmentation remains below threshold.
bn2.weight=0.1 avoided full zero-gamma collapse but still plateaued at 93.64%, so residual identity bias remains below anchor.
A smooth 0.01-to-0.002 tail preserved the first drop and reached 93.87%, but did not beat the flat-tail anchor.

column5: Batch size 160 on label-smoothed reflection anchor
column6: A larger batch preserved the first LR drop and improved coverage, but peaked at 93.71%, confirming batch-size deviations lag the 128 anchor.
Training-only residual stochastic depth preserved the LR drop, but plateaued at 93.40%, making this residual regularizer weaker than the anchor.
Mixup completed cleanly and reached the LR drop, but peaked at 93.85%, so label-space interpolation remains below the anchor.

column5: Strong weight decay on weights only
column6: Excluding BatchNorm and bias from 2e-4 decay preserved throughput but peaked at 93.68%, so global coupled decay remains better.
Turning label smoothing off after the first LR drop collapsed training loss but peaked at 93.42%, so late hard-label sharpening overfits.
Adding SE gates preserved the LR drop but peaked at 93.71%, so channel recalibration lags the current anchor.
Average-pool shortcut downsampling preserved throughput and LR timing but plateaued at 93.42%, so smoothing transition shortcuts lags strided option-A.

column5: Mixup alpha 0.1 without extra label smoothing
column6: Removing endpoint label smoothing from mild mixup still peaked at 93.81%, so the mixup mechanism remains below the 2e-4 anchor.
Head-only dropout preserved throughput and LR timing but peaked at 93.54%, so classifier feature dropout weakens the current anchor.
Shallower wider ResNet-14 reached 51,471 steps but peaked at 93.51%, so reduced depth loses too much representation despite speed.
Layer3-only SE preserved the LR drop but peaked at 93.26%, worse than all-block SE and the anchor, so SE is not promising here.
Probabilistic CutMix reached 94.11%, clearing the +0.10pp threshold while beating direct mixup and Cutout variants.
Lowering CutMix probability to 0.25 reached 94.09%, just below the 94.11 baseline, so p=0.5 remains the CutMix anchor.
Raising CutMix probability to 0.75 tied the 94.11% baseline but missed the 94.21% noise-guard threshold, so p=0.5 remains best.
Lowering CutMix alpha to 0.5 peaked at 94.07%, below the 94.21% threshold, so alpha=1.0 remains the best CutMix anchor.
Raising CutMix alpha to 2.0 peaked at 94.00%, below the 94.21% threshold, so alpha=1.0 remains the local CutMix anchor.
Reducing CutMix probability to 0.25 after the first LR drop peaked at 93.73%, so late CutMix tapering weakens the current anchor.
Standard CIFAR channel std badly miscalibrated the CutMix anchor, peaking at 75.03%, so keep unit-std input scaling.
CIFAR AutoAugment stacked with CutMix peaked at 93.62%, below baseline, so policy augmentation over-regularizes the current anchor.
Fan-out Conv2d Kaiming reached 94.16%, a small +0.05pp over baseline but below the 94.21% noise guard.
A 2000-step clean warmup peaked at 94.14%, above baseline but below the 94.21% noise guard, so static CutMix remains preferable.
Hard-label CutMix endpoints reached 94.17%, above baseline but below the 94.21% noise guard, so endpoint smoothing is not the missing lever.

A 500-step LR warmup peaked at 94.08%, below baseline and threshold, so early optimizer warmup is not the missing stability lever.

Raising horizontal flip probability to 0.45 regressed to 94.05%, closing the local flip bracket around the 0.4 anchor.
